review: The hymn is the greatness of the love: 1:1–6 is Eph 3:18–19 with 1 John 4:10, 2:1–6 is Rom 5:8 with Hos 13:14 (the ransoming of ruin) and John 10:18, and 3:1–6 is 1 John 4:19 (הוּא אָהַב אֹתָנוּ תְּחִלָּה) with Rom 12:1.

2:5–6 are the divine speech of the print («سَفَكْتُ بِالْحُبِّ دَمِي / مَا رَدُّ حُبِّي يَا تُرَى؟»); the Hebrew keeps the first person and the unanswered question, using the colon at 2:4 as the glossary requires instead of quotation marks.

2:3 שָׁבְתָה אֶת־כָּל־הַכִּלָּיוֹן — the Arabic أَسْرَى الرَّدَى جَمِيعَهُم takes 'ruin' captive; the Hebrew uses שָׁבָה (Judg 5:12) with כִּלָּיוֹן (Isa 10:23), so the line says the love has disarmed destruction itself.
